Welcome

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. The “Learn more” button above demonstrates smooth transitions and proper visual feedback.

Try using the Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference
  • HTML Living Standard
  • A11y 101

content.text:
`0.html` was already in good shape: it had solid accessibility, dark mode, reduced-motion handling and print styles. I made four small edits to it, but I haven't opened it in a browser to check how they look.

1. **Anchor jumps:** Sections now have `scroll-margin-top`, so the "Learn more" link to `#resources` stops with a little space above the heading instead of pressing it against the top of the window.
2. **High-contrast mode:** In Windows High Contrast (forced colors), browsers can remove the background from the skip link and buttons, which makes them hard to see. They now get a visible system-colored border in that mode.
3. **Cleanup:**
   - Removed a `padding` line on `body` that the four per-side `padding-*` lines right after it were overriding anyway.
   - Removed the `robots` meta tag. `index, follow` is what search engines do by default, so it had no effect.
4. **List spacing:** List items had a 0.75rem gap between them, which looked loose. I reduced it to 0.5rem and removed a `line-height` that just repeated the inherited value.

My first try used a Python script to make all the edits at once, but it needed approval and was denied automatically. I made the same changes with the file editor instead, except one: a redundant `[id]:target` rule the script would have added.

`0.html` was already in good shape: it had solid accessibility, dark mode, reduced-motion handling and print styles. I made four small edits to it, but I haven't opened it in a browser to check how they look.

1. **Anchor jumps:** Sections now have `scroll-margin-top`, so the "Learn more" link to `#resources` stops with a little space above the heading instead of pressing it against the top of the window.
2. **High-contrast mode:** In Windows High Contrast (forced colors), browsers can remove the background from the skip link and buttons, which makes them hard to see. They now get a visible system-colored border in that mode.
3. **Cleanup:**
   - Removed a `padding` line on `body` that the four per-side `padding-*` lines right after it were overriding anyway.
   - Removed the `robots` meta tag. `index, follow` is what search engines do by default, so it had no effect.
4. **List spacing:** List items had a 0.75rem gap between them, which looked loose. I reduced it to 0.5rem and removed a `line-height` that just repeated the inherited value.

My first try used a Python script to make all the edits at once, but it needed approval and was denied automatically. I made the same changes with the file editor instead, except one: a redundant `[id]:target` rule the script would have added.
